boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of California-Irvine, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop through UCI’s central campus: orient yourself, pause at landmarks, and identify useful study and student spaces.

cards.title: Start in Aldrich Park
cards.subtitle: First stop: the campus center
cards.notes: Walk a short section of the park first, then use its paths and surrounding schools to get oriented before choosing your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A central green starting point for learning the campus layout.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI identifies Aldrich Park as the center of campus and says Ring Road circles the park, with undergraduate schools placed along it.
cards.source_title: Aldrich Park | Office of Undergraduate Admissions | UCI
cards.access_notes: Follow posted campus guidance and use public paths.

cards.title: Trace the Ring Road loop
cards.subtitle: Second stop: orient around the central park
cards.notes: Use the circular path to connect a few academic plazas rather than trying to see every building at once; note the routes you will repeat.
cards.short_summary: The campus’s main circular route around Aldrich Park.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI states that Ring Road is the circular path surrounding Aldrich Park and that plazas connect the schools to the park.
cards.source_title: Aldrich Park | Office of Undergraduate Admissions | UCI
cards.access_notes: A pedestrian route; yield and follow campus wayfinding.

cards.title: Pause at Infinity Fountain
cards.subtitle: Third stop: a Physical Sciences landmark
cards.notes: Make this a quick photo-and-meetup point, then check which nearby buildings match your schedule or interests for the coming week.
cards.short_summary: A named fountain in a plaza near Physical Sciences.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI places the Infinity Fountain in a small plaza near the School of Physical Sciences and describes it as a place for meet-ups and studying.
cards.source_title: Aldrich Park | Office of Undergraduate Admissions | UCI

cards.title: Visit the Jao Family Sculpture Garden
cards.subtitle: Fourth stop: below Humanities Plaza
cards.notes: Take a quiet lap through the garden and save the location for a future between-class pause; stay on designated walking areas.
cards.short_summary: A sculpture garden associated with Humanities Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI states that the Jao Family Sculpture Garden is below Humanities Plaza and celebrates notable Chinese philosophers.
cards.source_title: Aldrich Park | Office of Undergraduate Admissions | UCI
cards.access_notes: Outdoor visit; observe posted rules and protect the artworks.

cards.title: Get your bearings at the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Fifth stop: services, gathering, and study spaces
cards.notes: Stop at the Information Center for campus direction help, then locate the study areas and building entrances you may use during the quarter.
cards.short_summary: A student-services and study hub with an Information Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCI Student Center page says the building includes study spaces, and its Information Center page identifies it as building 113 on the campus map.
cards.source_title: Information Center | UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: The Information Center lists Student Center building hours as 7:00 a.m.–midnight daily, except university holidays.

cards.title: Locate Anteater Plaza
cards.subtitle: Sixth stop: beside the Student Center
cards.notes: Use the plaza as a waypoint between the Student Center, Aldrich Hall, Langson Library, and food or bookstore entrances shown on the diagram.
cards.short_summary: A named plaza in the Student Center Ring Mall area.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Student Center’s Ring Mall diagram labels Anteater Plaza and shows it adjacent to the Student Center, Aldrich Hall, Langson Library, The Hill, and Zot N Go.
cards.source_title: Ring Mall Spaces | UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Use the plaza as a pedestrian waypoint and keep event setups clear.

cards.title: Find The Hill for course supplies
cards.subtitle: Seventh stop: Anteater Plaza storefront
cards.notes: Identify the storefront now so you can return when a class asks for materials; confirm any needed items and costs before purchasing.
cards.short_summary: A named campus bookstore destination at Anteater Plaza.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Student Center’s Ring Mall diagram labels The Hill at Anteater Plaza near the Student Center.
cards.source_title: Ring Mall Spaces | UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Retail availability and item pricing vary; check before purchase.

cards.title: Make a first pass through Langson Library
cards.subtitle: Eighth stop: humanities and social-sciences research
cards.notes: Locate the checkout desk and one floor that suits quiet reading, then bookmark the study-space locator for a later reservation if needed.
cards.short_summary: A UCI library supporting arts, humanities, education, social sciences, business, and management.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries states that Langson Library supports research and teaching in the arts, humanities, education, social sciences, social ecology, business, and management.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms are reservable through the UCI Libraries Study Space Locator.

cards.title: Scope out Gateway Study Center
cards.subtitle: Ninth stop: study rooms and collaborative workspaces
cards.notes: Check the second-floor layout and plan a future group session; use the Study Space Locator when you need a room rather than assuming one is open.
cards.short_summary: A library study center with computer, room, and collaborative-work options.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries states that Gateway Study Center’s second floor houses a computer lab, study rooms, and collaborative workspaces.
cards.source_title: Gateway Study Center | UC Irvine Libraries
cards.access_notes: Computer access requires a valid UCInetID; study-room reservations have eligibility and time rules.

cards.title: End with a Science Library study plan
cards.subtitle: Tenth stop: collaborative and quiet-floor options
cards.notes: Compare the fifth-floor collaborative areas with the designated quiet floors, then reserve a group room only when your group has a clear work plan.
cards.short_summary: A science-focused library with reservable rooms and distinct study settings.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries says the Science Library’s fifth floor has collaborative work areas, while its fourth and sixth floors are designated quiet floors.
cards.access_notes: Group study rooms require reservations through the Study Space Locator.
